# Historical scene execution audit

**Scope and provenance.** The principal cases are C1 test scenes `commons_155212263` and `commons_16007442`. For compact citations, `T/<scene>/<file>` means the original expanded file under `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/`. Every cited test file is also in `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/work/scene_archive/bundles/ablation_r1--generic_same_structured_evidence.tar.gz`, at member `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/generic_same_structured_evidence/C1/test/<scene>/<file>`. Citations give source IDs and exact original lines.

## Metalworking workshop

**Code intent and representation.** The selected step-3 build groups editable boxes, rods and 24-segment swept rings into floorboards, windows, a long timber bench, lathe, flywheel, anvil, vises, drawer and inventory. The anvil is a timber block plus stacked boxes, six tapered rod sections and a heel; the flywheel has two rims and six curved spokes. These are constructed approximations, not measured reference geometry or proof of contact between parts [X0177, T/commons_155212263/steps/003/build.py, lines 30–48, 95–163, 176–195].

The code comments describe a prior render as too distant and pale; step 3 moves the camera to (5, −4.2, 3.65), targets (−0.80, 0.15, 1.12), retains a 43 mm lens and reduces daylight/fill to 450/65. Those comments are reported review claims, not independently observed image quality [X0177, lines 7–21]. Global material operations add noise-driven color ramps and bump, roughness 0.82, and conditional metallic 0.40; qualifying window materials are copied before emission edits. Three area lights, a 0.18-strength world, Eevee Next, 512×384 PNG and AgX medium-high contrast are specified [X0177, lines 265–327].

**Execution and validation.** Step 1 requested Cycles with 48 samples but timed out after approximately 600 seconds, with no image and empty captured output; the failure phase is unknown [X0173, T/commons_155212263/steps/001/build.py, lines 318–329; X0174, T/commons_155212263/steps/001/result.json, lines 2–7]. The step-2 repair reduced primitive/path complexity and removed procedural material graphs; its result reports success and a saved image. Step 3 likewise reports success, empty stderr, a saved PNG and blend file; its render log records 16 samples and 20.46 seconds. The log’s render behavior should not be conflated with the build’s Eevee setting: it is separately reported execution evidence [X0175, T/commons_155212263/steps/002/build.py, lines 31–48; X0176, T/commons_155212263/steps/002/result.json, lines 2–7; X0178, T/commons_155212263/steps/003/result.json, lines 2–7].

`selected.json` records step 3. The record reports valid and functional passes for the anvil, but explicitly limits functional interpretation to structural/edit operability; semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null. Its overall score is 0.4325, SSIM 0.1454 and LPIPS 0.7022—not independent proof of fidelity [X0171, T/commons_155212263/selected.json, line 2; X0170, T/commons_155212263/record.json, lines 16–34].

## Electronics workbench

**Code intent.** The final build constructs a wall-backed bench with drawer cabinets, rotated monitor and keyboard, oscilloscope, tilted meter, three individually rotated notebook pages, soldering station, lamp and segmented test leads. It uses boxes and rods rather than the first attempt’s fillets and dense sweeps; coordinates and shared endpoints do not establish physical connections [X0180, T/commons_16007442/build.py, lines 29–42, 47–106, 131–158, 188–210, 223–232, 243–263; X0186, T/commons_16007442/steps/002/build.py, lines 18–42].

The final code describes tightening the earlier framing and darkening surfaces, sets a 47 mm lens, camera (0.18, −3.25, 2.68), two area lights at 135/40, world strength 0.18, global roughness 0.57, Eevee Next and 512×388 PNG. It specifies no procedural texture graph [X0180, lines 8–18, 303–329].

**Execution and selection.** Step 1 requested Cycles, 32 samples and denoising, but timed out at approximately 600 seconds without an image [X0184, T/commons_16007442/steps/001/build.py, lines 356–364; X0185, T/commons_16007442/steps/001/result.json, lines 2–7]. Step 2 is explicitly a runtime repair, and the final build comments refer to a successful render; however, no step-2 or step-3 result log is supplied here, so their individual successful execution cannot be independently confirmed from those logs. Step 3 is recorded as selected, and the run record says complete, valid and functional-pass for `bench_papers`, with completeness and collision truth null; overall is 0.4996, SSIM 0.1656 and LPIPS 0.5826 [X0186, lines 18–19; X0180, lines 8–13; X0182, T/commons_16007442/selected.json, line 2; X0181, T/commons_16007442/record.json, lines 16–34, 47–53].

**Quality boundary.** No reference or rendered image is attached. Thus neither case’s visual similarity, actual part contact, nor the claimed framing improvements can be visually verified. A completed run or numeric acceptance is distinct from a technically failed timeout and can still be a poor reconstruction.
